episodes.205920: A waterspout was reported on the west side of Galveston Bay.
episodes.206340: Within an area of uncapped 1500 J/kg MLCAPE, less than 20 knots of effective shear, and decent mid-level lapse rates near 6-6.5 C/km, some scattered thunderstorms developed off of remnant outflow and weak convergence along a stalled boundary. Despite the weak shear, favorable CAPE profiles supported a sufficiently strong and long-lived updraft to produce quarter size hail.
episodes.206400: In the early afternoon of the 19th, a cold front moving over northwestern Kansas caused  a few isolated storms to form that generally moved south-southeast, except one supercell that moved almost due east over Oberlin then moved south.  This single storm was the source for the storm reports. Hail up to 2.25 inches were reported, the largest falling in eastern Sheridan County.  The strongest reported gust was 69 MPH near Quinter.
episodes.206537: An upper-level disturbance interacting with a nearly stationary frontal boundary triggered clusters of strong thunderstorms across central Illinois during the afternoon of September 20th.  A storm cell intersecting an outflow boundary over Mason County resulted in an EF-0 tornado east of Mason City.  Meanwhile other storms produced hail as large as quarters and isolated minor wind damage.
episodes.206646: Widespread daytime and evening thunderstorm activity impacted the WFO Norman Forecast Area on the 20th. This activity was influenced by two factors: 1.) a weak surface low and associated front, and 2.) a remnant mesoscale convective vortex (MCV) across the Red River Valley. Despite relatively weak wind shear across most of the area, slightly stronger daytime instability across the former regime promoted more robust convection (and associated severe outcomes). Damaging wind gusts and a few instances of large hail were observed with this activity.
episodes.206884: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across western Kansas during the evening of the 19th, near a surface low pressure system and frontal boundary. These storms moved east-southeast, and into northeastern Oklahoma during the early morning hours of the 20th. The strongest storms produced damaging wind gusts. Another round of thunderstorms developed over northern Oklahoma during the evening of the 20th, along the stalled frontal boundary. These storms moved east across portions of northeastern Oklahoma during the late evening hours. The strongest storms produced large hail up to golf ball size and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.207005: An environment consisting of modest instability (1000 J/kg SBCAPE) and weak shear supported a couple of strong storms as they moved northeast through Wayne county. One storm produced strong winds north of Fairfield.
episodes.207032: Scattered thunderstorms tracked through the region during the early morning hours on Saturday (9/20).  One storm produced an isolated wind gust to 60 mph in Oshkosh.
episodes.207033: Thunderstorms developed ahead of a weakening occluded front during the late afternoon and early evening hours on Saturday (9/20).  The storms produced small hail and damaging winds across east-central Wisconsin.
episodes.207123: Isolated storms materialized in the afternoon and evening hours of September 20th, with activity focused on primarily the eastern to central Panhandles. This is where conditions were favorable for activity to become severe with large hail and damaging winds. A couple of potentially severe storms traversed the northeast Panhandles near Perryton and Beaver, but the only confirmed instances of severe weather took place with a slow moving cell cluster just east of Amarillo. Here, damaging winds of 65 to 75 mph resulted in some damage. In addition, accumulating hail occurred just to the east of Amarillo.
episodes.207435: A front moved through the region with heavy rain on the evening of the 19th followed by heavy showers through the 20th. The heavy rainfall rates resulted in two landslides along Auke Lake in Juneau.
episodes.207449: An upper-level wave moved across the Great plains and supported the development of supercells. There was only a small window for severe weather from each supercell moved south before weakening. After all the cells had weakened below severe and developed a small cold pool, they congealed and followed a more linear structure that tracked east.
episodes.207586: An approaching 50+ knot jet and a mid level disturbance contributed to strong to severe thunderstorms developing along the Rio Grande Valley.  Flash flooding was reported near Radium Springs and severe wind gusts near Percha Creek.
episodes.207587: An approaching upper level jet and a weak shortwave at the mid levels helped thunderstorms to develop in an environment with deep moisture in place.  Heavy rain was reported around El Paso county with the airport receiving almost 2 inches in an hour and a half.
episodes.207595: A deep tropical moisture surge contributed to the generation of showers and thunderstorms. As rain accumulated, soil became saturated, and flooding and landslides were registered. Also, wind and lightning damage was also observed within the thunderstorms.
episodes.207617: Widespread pulse thunderstorms produced locally heavy rain across the Midlands, including isolated flash flooding in the Columbia metro in the evening of September 20th. Above average precipitable water, a weak approaching trough, and little wind shear produced slow moving storms with highly efficient rain rates of 3-4 inches per hour.
episodes.207746: A northward moving warm front interacted with limited instability and shear to produce a line of showers and thunderstorms. While most remained below severe levels, one storm produced an isolated downburst with some localized damage reported.
episodes.207747: A northward moving warm front interacted with limited instability and shear to produce a line of showers and thunderstorms. While most remained below severe levels, one storm gained sufficient strength to produce marginally severe hail.
episodes.207765: Deep moisture ahead of an approaching upper trough resulted in thunderstorms that were efficient rain producers.
episodes.207846: A strong thunderstorm produced hail up the three-quarter inch in Lincoln County, just  north of Pumkin Center.
episodes.207870: Moisture from the remnants of Pacific Tropical Storm Mario fueled scattered thunderstorms, many of which produced flash flooding.

The City & Borough of Juneau Parks and Recreation teams closed the Auke Lake Trail on Saturday after two landslides were observed. The first landslide was reported via social media at approximately 130pm AKDT on the 20th between the two docks at Auke Lake. The second reported landslide via social media occurred at approximately 235pm AKDT. Rainfall amounts in the 12 hours leading up to the slides were 1-2 inches in vicinity of Auke Bay. Jordan Creek and Montana Creek areas also saw minor flooding during this time. The trail along the lake remained closed for the next two months.
